headline: Domestic growth remains supportive under a neutral policy stance, but uneven inflation and unverified external prices argue for franchise-quality equity exposure rather than a broad cyclical beta call.
base_case: Real activity stays constructive over 6–12 months without mechanically extrapolating the strong Q1 FY2026-27 GDP print.
RBI remains data-dependent around a 5.25% repo and neutral stance; funding-cost relief is gradual, not a rapid easing cycle.
Equity returns stay stock- and sector-specific: de-rating risk persists where earnings visibility is weak.
Public capex execution continues to support order books in capital goods and infrastructure-linked suppliers.
upside: Food inflation cools faster than feared, opening room for policy support without a growth scare.
Capex crowding-in lifts private investment and utilisation more than budgeted outlays alone imply.
Global risk appetite stabilises, reducing INR and imported-input stress for domestic franchises.
downside: Food or oil shocks prolong inflation persistence and delay any easing path.
Global risk-off tightens financial conditions and pressures the currency and import-intensive margins.
Capex or earnings delivery misses force further de-rating in crowded quality/growth names.
transmission_map: Domestic GDP and public capex → demand and order books for banks, NBFCs, capital goods and selective industrials.
CPI path + neutral MPC → deposit pricing, NIM discipline and the speed of rate-sensitive recovery in realty/autos.
Liquidity and funding conditions → lender ALM outcomes; one-day surplus/absorption prints are not a durable trend.
Crude / INR (unverified at cutoff) → treat as two-sided margin and external-balance risks, not as embedded price targets.
Global demand and discount-rate volatility → selectivity for IT/metals exporters versus domestic compounders.
Net transmission → prefer balance-sheet strength, liability franchise and execution visibility (Banks, Pharma, Capital Goods OW leans).
portfolio_implications: Keep Banks OW expressed through scaled franchises and selected challengers — deposit competition matters more than a rate-cut beta trade.
Keep Pharma/Healthcare OW as a defensive growth sleeve where domestic and specialty mix can offset export regulatory noise.
Maintain Capital Goods / Infrastructure OW as a capex-execution sleeve; watch order conversion and working-capital stress.
Stay selective on IT and metals until external demand and global risk appetite are clearer.
Do not treat trailing index weakness alone as valuation support without verified earnings revisions.

risk_watchlist.title: Food inflation persistence
risk_watchlist.note: August 2026 CPI showed food running above headline; prolongs purchasing-power and policy uncertainty.

risk_watchlist.title: Deposit competition / NIM pressure
risk_watchlist.note: Neutral policy stance elevates liability franchise quality over wholesale-funded growth.

risk_watchlist.title: Oil and external price shocks
risk_watchlist.note: Cutoff crude print: Data unavailable from reliable sources. Treat oil as a two-sided inflation and margin risk.

risk_watchlist.title: INR and portfolio flow volatility
risk_watchlist.note: Cutoff FX/flow print: Data unavailable from reliable sources. Monitor yields, oil and risk-appetite transmission.

risk_watchlist.title: Public/private capex execution slips
risk_watchlist.note: Budgeted outlays help, but order books and utilisation depend on execution quality.

risk_watchlist.title: Earnings visibility / de-rating
risk_watchlist.note: Without verified forward earnings breadth, price correction is not automatic undervaluation.
